title: Transportability of the microaxial flow pump trial result to unselected AMI-CS: target trial emulation by DanGer Shock eligibility, age and sex

pico.population: Adults with acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock in UK registries (BCIS, ICNARC, Harefield), split into DanGer Shock-eligible and non-eligible strata (NSTEMI-CS, out-of-hospital arrest, mixed shock, older age, women)
pico.comparator: Standard care without a microaxial flow pump
pico.outcomes: All-cause mortality at 30 days and 180 days; severe bleeding, renal replacement therapy
pico.timing: Time zero at the point of eligibility (shock diagnosis with revascularisation decision), clone-censor-weight design

decision: Whether to place a microaxial flow pump in AMI-CS patients outside the DanGer Shock inclusion criteria, in patients aged 77 years or older, and in women.
why_now: The only randomised trial of the pump (38587239, 355 analysed) showed lower death in the whole population, while prespecified or exploratory analyses suggest less apparent benefit in older patients (39551167, P for interaction = 0.028) and women (41222528, P for interaction = 0.18), and a national registry reports that eligible patients were 35.6% of Impella-treated AMI-CS (41078250). Renal replacement therapy was more frequent with the pump (39462276).

competing.note: DOUBLE-SHOCK, routine microaxial pump plus pulmonary artery catheter monitoring versus standard care in heart attack-related shock; reports after the 24-month window (registry primary outcome field not recorded in the store)

designs.primary: Target trial emulation in linked BCIS-ICNARC data with Harefield pump registry data, benchmarked first against the DanGer Shock result in eligible patients, then extended to non-eligible strata
designs.alternative: Registry-based randomised trial of pump use in non-eligible strata, embedded in the planned UK shock platform

data_required: Linked national AMI-CS registry data with device exposure, haemodynamics, lactate, arrest status and 180-day mortality.
feasibility: Data access runs through collaborators; Harefield registry is held. Benchmarking against the randomised estimate is the main de-risking step. Confounding by indication in shock is severe, so the design will stand only if the benchmark reproduces the trial result.
overlap: Partial overlap with the owner's Markov microsimulation of microaxial support in STEMI-related shock; this question supplies effect estimates for non-eligible strata that the model currently lacks. No overlap with the temporary right ventricular assist device SRMA.

G1.note: Pump use in shock is a high-mortality decision made routinely outside trial criteria.

G2.note: Judged on trial evidence only: a single trial exists, with no randomised data in non-eligible strata; guideline position unverified.

G3.note: The only competing trial in the trials file on the pump, NCT07762560, has primary completion 2030-10, beyond 24 months. The Lancet IPD meta-analysis 39236726 (published 2024-09-14) covers early unselected mechanical support, not the eligibility strata proposed here.

G4.note: A benchmarked emulation is citable by a guideline committee only if it reproduces the randomised estimate; a plain registry comparison would not be, because of confounding by indication.

G5.note: Not a repeat synthesis; it tests transportability and effect modification that the trial could not.

impact.why: AMI-CS is high-mortality and the pump is used widely beyond trial criteria.

novelty.why: Benchmarked emulation for non-eligible strata has not been reported in the appraised subset.

equipoise.why: Trial evidence is positive overall but absent or contradictory in older, female and non-STEMI patients.

design.why: Strong identification is hard in shock; benchmarking mitigates but does not remove the risk.

timeliness.why: Practice is expanding after DanGer Shock and the next trial reports after 2030.

citation.why: Shock device questions in the target journals attract high attention, though no benchmark figures were drawn for this synthesis.

feasibility.why: Owner holds registry access and collaborators.

next_actions: Draft the emulation protocol with eligibility mapped to DanGer Shock criteria and register it.
Confirm variable availability and linkage permissions with BCIS and ICNARC collaborators.
Run the benchmarking emulation on the eligible stratum before any extension.

title: Pre-registered prospective synthesis of early left ventricular unloading during VA-ECMO, timed to the pending randomised readouts

pico.population: Adults with cardiogenic shock supported with peripheral VA-ECMO
pico.intervention: Early left ventricular unloading (microaxial pump, balloon pump or other)
pico.outcomes: All-cause mortality at 30 days; bleeding, haemolysis, vascular complications
pico.timing: Unloading at or within hours of ECMO initiation

decision: Whether to unload the left ventricle routinely when VA-ECMO is started.
why_now: Observational data associate unloading with lower mortality (30765031, RR 0.79; 33032450, HR 0.79; 35361346, aOR 0.84) but the one reported randomised trial did not differ (37850383, 116 patients, HR 1.02). Several randomised trials are due to report in 2027.

competing.note: REMAP ECMO, unloading in VA-ECMO (registry primary outcome field not recorded in the store)
EULODIA, early preventive unloading after VA-ECMO (registry primary outcome field not recorded in the store)
EASE-ECMO, early balloon pump after VA-ECMO (registry primary outcome field not recorded in the store)

gap_type: underpowered trials; conflicting observational and randomised evidence

designs.primary: Prospective meta-analysis with pre-specified protocol and IPD request, registered before the readouts
designs.alternative: Reconstructed-IPD analysis once trial curves are published, with Bayesian pooling

data_required: IPD or Kaplan-Meier curves from the unloading trials.
data_sources: Trial groups of NCT05913622, NCT07027202, NCT06872021
feasibility: Fits the owner's same-day synthesis workflow; IPD access needs trial group agreement.
overlap: Adjacent to the owner's review of acute MR and shock and to same-day congress SRMAs; no duplicate of an active project.

G1.note: Routine unloading is a common decision in a high-mortality setting.

G2.note: Observational and randomised results conflict; guideline position unverified.

G3.note: REMAP ECMO (430, 2027-07) and EULODIA (298, 2027-07) are adequately sized trials of the same comparison expected within 24 months; the synthesis would follow rather than precede an answer.

G4.note: A prospective meta-analysis of registered trials is citable by guideline committees.

G5.note: Pooling is pre-specified before the new data. The existing Lancet IPD analysis 39236726 pooled five trials of left ventricular unloading devices (503 patients) and four VA-ECMO trials, so the new synthesis must add the pending trials and a distinct unloading-on-ECMO question to avoid repeating it.

impact.why: VA-ECMO for shock is used less often than pump or revascularisation decisions.

novelty.why: Prospective pooling of unloading trials has not appeared in the appraised subset.

timeliness.why: Three trials report within about 12 to 24 months.

citation.why: Synthesis of small trials rarely reaches the top decile unless the result is decisive.

next_actions: Check each trial's registered primary outcome and contact trial groups about IPD sharing.
Write the protocol and register it on PROSPERO before any readout.
Pre-specify the update workflow and the effect-modification analyses.

status_history.reason: Proposed from the D2 landscape synthesis (appraised subset only).

title: Regional shock networks and specialist-centre care for cardiogenic shock: natural-experiment analysis of outcomes after network introduction

pico.population: Adults admitted with cardiogenic shock in UK hospitals (BCIS and ICNARC linked data)
pico.intervention: Admission to or transfer to a centre or region operating a formal shock team or hub-and-spoke pathway
pico.comparator: Care in centres or regions without such a pathway, with staggered introduction as the natural experiment
pico.outcomes: In-hospital and 180-day mortality; use of invasive haemodynamics and mechanical support
pico.timing: Before and after pathway introduction, stepped by region

decision: Whether commissioners should centralise cardiogenic shock care and mandate shock-team pathways.
decision_maker: Health systems, commissioners and cardiac network leads
why_now: Observational data associate shock teams with lower CICU mortality (34556316, adjusted OR 0.72; 95% CI 0.55-0.94), an AHA statement addresses critical care cardiology structure (39945062, 40249352) and no randomised comparison exists in the appraised subset.

competing.note: DIGI-CS, digital out-of-hospital management in early shock; a different intervention, listed for context (registry primary outcome field not recorded in the store)

designs.primary: Staggered difference-in-differences or synthetic control analysis using linked registry data
designs.alternative: Stepped-wedge cluster trial embedded in the registry platform

data_required: Dated records of pathway introduction by centre and region, linked patient-level outcomes.
feasibility: Depends on reliable dates of pathway introduction; feasible through collaborators.
overlap: Substantial overlap with the owner's SRMA of cardiogenic shock care organisation. This candidate is original research that would follow that review, and should not proceed unless the SRMA leaves the effect unresolved.

G1.note: Organisation of shock care affects every shock admission.

G2.note: Only observational association is present in the appraised subset; guideline position unverified.

G3.note: No competing trial of the same question appears in the trials file; the owner's SRMA is unpublished.

G4.note: Staggered rollouts in the UK may be too few and too confounded by concurrent practice change to support a causal estimate that a committee would cite.

G5.note: A natural-experiment analysis is not a repeat synthesis or a single-centre series.

novelty.why: Observational shock-team associations exist; causal designs are scarce.

equipoise.why: Direction of effect is likely favourable but unproven.

design.why: Identification depends on the rollout pattern.

timeliness.why: Network development is active but no readout is pending.

citation.why: Systems papers can perform in JAMA Cardiology if the design is strong.

next_actions: Wait for the owner's SRMA of shock care organisation to define the residual gap.
Map pathway introduction dates across UK centres.
Test whether the rollout pattern supports a staggered design.

status_history.reason: Proposed from the D2 landscape synthesis (appraised subset only).

title: Pre-specified individual patient data analysis of immediate versus delayed angiography after cardiac arrest without ST elevation, updated for the DISCO readout

pico.population: Resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest without ST-segment elevation
pico.comparator: Delayed or selective angiography after intensive care assessment
pico.outcomes: Survival and neurological outcome at 30 and 90 days; long-term survival

decision: Whether to perform immediate angiography in resuscitated patients without ST elevation, and in which subgroups.
decision_maker: Cardiac arrest centres and interventional cardiologists
why_now: The network meta-analysis found benefit only in non-randomised studies (36300362, OR 0.89 in randomised trials; 95% CI 0.73-1.10). COACT 5-year follow-up showed 54.8% versus 51.8% alive (41636663). DISCO (NCT02309151, 1003 patients) has a registered primary completion of 2026-04.

competing.note: DISCO, direct or subacute angiography in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest; no results posted in the store (registry primary outcome field not recorded in the store)

gap_type: evidence outdated by a new trial; effect modification untested

designs.primary: IPD meta-analysis of randomised trials, with pre-specified tests of effect modification by rhythm, shock and ischaemic features
designs.alternative: Reconstructed-IPD analysis if IPD cannot be obtained

data_required: IPD from the angiography trials, including DISCO.
data_sources: Trial groups of the randomised angiography trials
feasibility: Requires IPD sharing from several European trial groups.
target_journal: European Heart Journal or JAMA Cardiology

G1.note: Post-arrest angiography is a common decision in a high-mortality setting.

G2.note: Randomised trials in the store did not differ; observational data conflict; guideline position unverified.

G3.note: DISCO (NCT02309151, 1003 patients) has a primary completion of 2026-04 and is an adequately sized randomised comparison of the same strategy. COACT randomised 552 (30883057) and a second trial 554 (34459570), so DISCO would add 1003 to about 1106 plus a 99-patient pilot (32985249), but the main comparison will be answered by DISCO first.

G4.note: IPD analysis with pre-specified subgroup tests is guideline-citable.

G5.note: Without a new effect-modification angle this is a repeat pooling of the same trials; it survives only if heterogeneity of treatment effect is the primary aim.

novelty.why: Pooled and network analyses already exist.

equipoise.why: Randomised data are neutral; observational data differ.

design.why: IPD is the strongest available design.

citation.why: Depends on whether DISCO is positive.

next_actions: Check the DISCO results status and primary report timing.
Contact trial groups about IPD sharing.
Decide whether an effect-modification aim justifies proceeding.

status_history.reason: Proposed from the D2 landscape synthesis (appraised subset only).

title: First-line inotrope and vasopressor strategy in SCAI stage C to D cardiogenic shock: registry-embedded multi-arm randomised trial

pico.population: Adults with cardiogenic shock of any cause requiring vasoactive support
pico.intervention: Pre-specified first-line inotrope strategies (for example dobutamine, milrinone, adrenaline with noradrenaline)
pico.comparator: Each other, with usual care in an observational reference arm
pico.outcomes: All-cause mortality at 30 days; refractory shock, arrhythmia

decision: Which inotrope to start first in cardiogenic shock.
why_now: The randomised data are small or neutral: epinephrine was stopped early for refractory shock (29976291, 57 patients), and milrinone did not differ from dobutamine (34347952, 192 participants). Trials of inotrope versus placebo and dopamine versus norepinephrine are registered but ask different questions.

competing.note: DOREMI-2, inotrope versus placebo; a different comparison (registry primary outcome field not recorded in the store)
ACTION-CS, norepinephrine versus dopamine; reports 2031 (registry primary outcome field not recorded in the store)
LevoHeartShock, levosimendan versus placebo (registry primary outcome field not recorded in the store)

gap_type: underpowered trials; strategy question industry will not fund

designs.primary: Registry-embedded multi-arm adaptive randomised trial in the planned UK shock platform
designs.alternative: Target trial emulation in BCIS and ICNARC data as a feasibility step

data_required: Registry platform with randomisation embedded, capture of vasoactive drug dose and duration.
feasibility: Consistent with the owner's registry trial platform aim, but the platform must be built first and needs funding.

G1.note: Vasoactive choice is made for almost every shock patient.

G2.note: Trials are small and neutral or stopped early; guideline position unverified.

G3.note: No registered trial in the file compares these specific inotrope strategies at adequate power; DOREMI-2 and ACTION-CS test different comparisons.

G4.note: A registry-embedded randomised trial would be citable, and an observational comparison would not because of confounding by indication.

G5.note: It is a new randomised comparison, not a repeat of pooled studies.

novelty.why: Individual comparisons have been tested at small scale.

equipoise.why: Randomised evidence is small and neutral.

design.why: Registry-embedded randomisation is established elsewhere in cardiology.

timeliness.why: Other vasoactive trials will report first and shape the arms.

citation.why: A large randomised shock trial would attract high attention.

next_actions: Review the registered protocols of DOREMI-2 and ACTION-CS to define non-overlapping arms.
Specify the registry fields needed for embedded randomisation.
Run a target trial emulation as a feasibility check.

status_history.reason: Proposed from the D2 landscape synthesis (appraised subset only).
